function: Learned (A2C) power allocation among NOMA users for massive IoT uplink access via a HAPS relay to a LEO satellite, maximizing system spectral efficiency (p. 10).
system: Uplink IoT UEs to HAPS to LEO satellite (600 km, Ka band, 7 clusters); generic multi-antenna Lu, Lhr, Lht, Ls, counts unspecified; no RIS (pp. 4, 12).
method: Reinforcement learning with Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C): one-hidden-layer actor (256 neurons) and critic (128), trained 150000 steps with reward equal to system rate (pp. 10-12).
data_channel: Own simulated channel: FSPL plus shadow fading for HAPS-satellite, LoS/NLoS probabilistic model for UE-HAPS from a UAV tutorial [48]; random UE placement; no dataset or measurement (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: Single simulator setting (Table II: 30 UEs/cluster, 3 active, K=3); curves swept over users per cluster (10-100) and cluster power (0.5-3 W); no separate train/test conditions stated (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Non-learned: S-ALOHA, SA-NOMA-SIC, SA-NOMA-JD [39], a random scheme. Learned: DRL-NSA [42] (DDPG), A3C, DDPG, DQN, Q-learning (pp. 12-14).
metrics: Successful access probability, system spectral efficiency (bps/Hz), reward and loss convergence, runtime per step as complexity (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Time complexity O(sum over layers of n_l * n_{l+1}) of the neural network; runtime per step compared with DDPG, A3C, DQN, Q-learning, random vs users (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 4: "we focus on FSPL and SF in large-scale fading". Custom FSPL, shadowing and LoS-probability channel (UE-HAPS model from UAV tutorial [48], p. 5); no 3GPP TR 38.811/38.901, DeepMIMO or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 14: "The number of users affects the state". Sweeps over users (Figs. 6-9, 13) and power (Fig. 14) are shown, but the paper never states that a model trained in one setting is tested in another or adapted.
q3_support: p. 12: "as well as the DRL-NSA scheme [42]." Learned baselines also A3C, DDPG, DQN, Q-learning (p. 14: "algorithm based on A2C outperforms A3C, DDPG, DQN"); non-learned S-ALOHA, SA-NOMA-SIC/JD [39] and a random scheme, on access probability and spectral efficiency.
q4_support: p. 13: "proposed RMA has a time complexity of". It gives O(sum n_l*n_{l+1}) over layers and compares measured runtime per step ("averaging the runtime per step of the algorithm", Fig. 12).
q5_support: p. 11: "Randomly generate users". Training and test data come from the paper's own simulator (Algorithm 2, channel of pp. 4-5); no code or data link, public dataset or measurement is mentioned.
notes: Learned part is only the A2C power allocation (p. 10); HAPS 3D deployment is solved by KKT and convex optimization (pp. 8-10), not learned. Included because learned power control in a satellite or aerial link is physical layer, so area 6. FSPL, clutter and shadow fading terms resemble TR 38.811 but no 3GPP document is cited, hence q1 is 0; reviewer may confirm.
